llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose matches the provided workflows, but there are configuration and security omissions (notably missing required env var metadata and no webhook HMAC verification) that make the package inconsistent or risky without changes.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, the five n8n workflows, and required capabilities (Shopify API, Google Sheets, SMTP) align with an order-management automation. All required binaries are none and there are no unexpected third-party services. However, the registry's required env list omits SHOPIFY_ORDERS_SHEET_ID which the SKILL.md and workflows use, creating an inconsistency between the skill metadata and the runtime instructions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the included n8n JSON files stay within the Shopify/order management scope (fetch orders, products, checkouts; log to Sheets; send emails). However: the webhook handler extracts the Shopify HMAC header (x-shopify-hmac-sha256) but does not verify it using SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET — the workflow exposes an endpoint that will accept and act on incoming POSTs without signature validation. The instructions also assume single-page fetches (products/orders limit=250) with no guidance for pagination, which can cause incomplete data. The abandoned-cart workflow sends emails to customers (make sure to follow anti-spam/consent rules).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files beyond n8n workflow JSON — low installation risk (nothing downloaded or written by an installer).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requested env vars (STORE URL, ACCESS_TOKEN, WEBHOOK_SECRET, ADMIN_EMAIL, LOW_STOCK_THRESHOLD) are appropriate for Shopify operations, and n8n credentials for Google Sheets and SMTP are expected. But SKILL.md and workflows also rely on SHOPIFY_ORDERS_SHEET_ID (and placeholders for n8n credential IDs) while that variable was not listed in the registry-required env list—metadata mismatch. The skill legitimately needs the Shopify access token, which is sensitive; the manifest doesn't mark a primary credential but that is informational rather than blocking.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true, does not modify other skills, and has no install-time persistent agents. It runs as n8n workflows and uses scheduled triggers; autonomous invocation of the skill by the agent platform is allowed by default but not extraordinary here.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This package is broadly what it says — a set of n8n workflows for Shopify order lifecycle automation — but do not install or deploy it as-is without fixes and operational checks. Specifically:

- Add SHOPIFY_ORDERS_SHEET_ID to the declared required env vars and provide the correct Google Sheets credential IDs and SMTP credential in n8n before importing.
- Fix webhook security: verify the x-shopify-hmac-sha256 header using SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET before trusting webhook payloads (current Parse Order code reads the header but does not validate it). Without signature verification an attacker could POST fake order payloads to your webhook URL.
- Protect your SHOPIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN: treat it as a secret, restrict app scopes and rotation, and run workflows in a network environment that limits exposure.
- Confirm email/legal compliance for abandoned-cart recovery (consent, unsubscribe links, anti-spam rules) and ensure SMTP credentials are used only for intended messages.
- Handle pagination for products/orders if your store has >250 items or >250 orders per query; the workflows use single-page requests and may miss data.
- Consider rate limits and error handling for Shopify API calls (retries, backoff) — workflows set timeouts but not robust error/backoff logic.

If you or the author address the webhook verification and the metadata omission, the skill appears coherent and usable. Until then classify it as suspicious because of the security-relevant omissions.
